PROG1.title: Introduction to C++
PROG1.content:
C++ Program Structure

Every C++ program begins execution at the main() function[cite: 1]. The structure relies on header files like iostream, namespaces, and statements[cite: 1].

Variables and Data Types

Variables are named storage locations used to store and manipulate data[cite: 1]. Common types include int for whole numbers, double for decimals, and string for text[cite: 1].

PROG2.title: Basic Syntax and Control Structures
PROG2.content:
Control Structures

Control structures determine the order in which statements execute[cite: 2, 5]. The three fundamental types are sequence, selection, and repetition[cite: 2, 5].

  • Selection: Uses if, else if, else, and switch[cite: 2, 5].
  • Repetition: Uses for, while, and do-while loops[cite: 2, 5].

PROG3.title: Functions
PROG3.content:
Modular Programming

Functions are reusable blocks of code written to perform a singular, specific task[cite: 3, 6].

  • Parameters & Arguments: Parameters are variables listed in a definition, while arguments are actual values supplied during a call[cite: 3].
  • Pass-by-Value: Receives a copy of the argument rather than the original variable[cite: 3].
